name: Chana Masala
summary: Chickpeas simmered in a tangy onion-tomato gravy with garam masala.
instructions: Finely chop the onions and tomatoes. Crush the ginger, garlic and green chilli into a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium heat and add the cumin seeds. Let them sizzle for 20 seconds.
Add the onions and cook, stirring often, until deep golden, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the ginger-garlic-chilli paste and cook for a minute until the raw smell goes.
Add turmeric and coriander powder with a splash of water so the spices don't burn.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt. Cook until they collapse and oil shows at the edges, 8–10 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and 1 cup of water. Mash a few chickpeas against the pan to thicken the gravy.
Simmer covered for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the garam masala and amchur, then taste and adjust the salt.
Finish with chopped coriander and serve with rice or roti.

name: Aloo Gobi
summary: Dry-spiced potato and cauliflower, cooked until just charred at the edges.
instructions: Cut the cauliflower into florets and the potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Rinse and drain well.
Heat the oil until it just smokes, then lower the heat and add the cumin.
Add the sliced onion and grated ginger and cook until soft.
Add the potatoes, turmeric and chilli powder. Toss to coat and cook covered for 5 minutes.
Add the cauliflower and salt, toss again, and cover. Cook on low heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring gently twice.
Add the chopped tomato and cook uncovered until the vegetables are tender and lightly charred.
Sprinkle garam masala, toss once more and serve hot.

name: Masoor Dal Tadka
summary: Red lentils cooked soft and finished with a sizzling ghee tempering.
instructions: Rinse the dal until the water runs clear.
Simmer the dal with 3 cups of water, turmeric and chopped tomato until completely soft, about 20 minutes.
Whisk the dal smooth and season with salt. Add hot water if it's too thick.
For the tadka, heat the ghee in a small pan and add the cumin.
When the cumin crackles, add sliced garlic and fry until golden.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the asafoetida and chilli powder.
Pour the tadka over the dal, squeeze in the lemon and serve.

name: Paneer Bhurji
summary: Crumbled paneer scrambled with onion, tomato and green chilli.
instructions: Crumble the paneer with your fingers and set aside.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the chopped onion and green chilli until soft.
Add the capsicum and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato, turmeric and salt, and cook until the tomato breaks down.
Fold in the paneer and garam masala and cook for 2–3 minutes, without letting it dry out.
Finish with coriander and serve with toast or roti.

name: Vegetable Upma
summary: Savoury semolina porridge with mustard seeds, curry leaves and vegetables.
instructions: Dry-roast the semolina in a pan over low heat until fragrant, then set it aside.
Heat the oil and add the mustard seeds. When they pop, add the urad dal and fry until golden.
Add the curry leaves, green chilli and onion, and cook until the onion is soft.
Add the diced carrot and peas and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in 2.5 cups of water with salt and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and pour in the semolina slowly, stirring all the time so no lumps form.
Cover and cook on low heat for 2 minutes, then fluff and serve.

name: Vegetable Stir Fry
summary: Crisp vegetables tossed in a soy-ginger sauce, served over rice.
instructions: Cut all the vegetables into thin, even strips so they cook at the same speed.
Heat the sesame oil in a wok over high heat.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the carrot and broccoli first, then the capsicum, onion and cabbage, stir-frying for 4–5 minutes.
Pour in the soy sauce and toss until everything is glossy but still crisp.
Serve straight away over the rice.

name: Chicken Stir Fry
summary: Quick-seared chicken with peppers and zucchini in a savoury sauce.
instructions: Slice the chicken thinly and toss it with 1 tbsp soy sauce and the corn flour.
Heat half the oil in a wok until very hot and sear the chicken in one layer until browned. Remove.
Add the remaining oil, then the garlic, carrot and broccoli. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the capsicum, onion and zucchini and stir-fry for 2 more minutes.
Return the chicken, add the remaining soy sauce and toss until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve hot with rice or noodles.

name: Quinoa Buddha Bowl
summary: Quinoa topped with roasted sweet potato, chickpeas, spinach and avocado.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Cube the sweet potato, toss with half the oil and salt, and roast for 25 minutes.
Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 cups of water for 15 minutes, then let it steam off the heat.
Toss the chickpeas in a hot pan until lightly crisp.
Whisk the remaining oil with lemon juice and a pinch of salt for the dressing.
Fill bowls with quinoa, spinach, grated carrot, sweet potato, chickpeas and sliced avocado, then dress.

name: Mushroom Risotto
summary: Creamy rice with mushrooms, peas and wilted spinach.
instructions: Brown the sliced mushrooms in half the butter and set them aside.
Soften the onion and garlic in the remaining butter.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the edges look translucent.
Add the stock one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed, for about 20 minutes.
Stir in the peas, spinach and mushrooms when the rice is nearly tender.
Take off the heat, beat in the cheese and rest for 2 minutes before serving.

name: Beef Tacos
summary: Spiced ground beef in warm tortillas with fresh toppings.
instructions: Brown the beef with the chopped onion, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the cumin, paprika, salt and a splash of water. Simmer until thick.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
Dice the tomato and avocado and shred the lettuce.
Fill each tortilla with beef and top with the vegetables, corn and cheese.
